light.notes: webkit's original warm-gray palette. Every override pins a role to the literal the hand-written stylesheet and present's graph and chart code carried before themes existed, so the default renders byte for byte as it did.

dark.notes: The semantic colours keep their light values, as the old dark block never overrode them, except purple, the one brightened in dark so purple text meets 3:1 on the chip surface (graph-module-4 keeps the old purple); the graph, chart, tag, and code roles pin the brighter literals app.js and the dark code block used. on-primary stays white (the old rules put #fff on every accent fill) while chip-active-text keeps the old dark literal, and the focus ring and the terracotta alias keep the light-mode values the old stylesheet never overrode in dark.

light.notes: Nord publishes no light variant; this one is built from its Snow Storm and Polar Night groups. bg nord5, paper nord6, chip nord4; border-hover derived (nord4 toward nord3); text-3 is nord3 brightened; aurora colours as published, pale on light

dark.notes: paper is the syntax background hsl(220,13%,18%); bg and chip are the One Dark UI panel steps; border the selection colour, border-hover the gutter; ink mono-1, mono-2, mono-3
